main_text.l: ἀναθήματα[?] dona & præsidia vanissimis idolis esse tribuenda.

Baltassar Rex Chaldeorū & Principes cū toto Gynecæo, è poculis sacris è tem-plo Hierosolymitano olim sublatis,in re-gali epulo biberūt vinum, & laudauerūt Deos aureos & argeteos, æreos,ferreos, ligneos & lapideos. Dan.5.4.

4. Opinio mendax, quasi qui ςωσφρονεῖ[?] habuit in rerum maximarum administra-tione, sine quorum opera & fide ne tantillum solus obtinere poterat, possit suæ solius prudentiæ, virtuti, dexteritati & alacritati, omnia illa ἀλογισμάτα[?] accepta ferre. Prudenter sanè Pyrrhus suis Aqui-lam in nubibus, ob res celeriter felicitér-que gestas vocantibus: Pervos, respon-dit, aquila sum. Qui enim non essem, qui vestris armis veluti pennis subleuer? Vi-tauit invidiā laude in commilitones trans-lata, non autem sibi uni vindicata.

5. Amentia & cæcitas tanta, ut ne qui-dem ἀλλοτρίων[?] alienarum calamitatum,no-bis persuadeat etiam nos homines esse, & multiplicibus casibus obnoxios, nec etiam meliore quam illi calamitosi, fortuna dignos. Vere dixit Menander:

page.notes: The first line is a continuation from the previous page (cont="true"). Greek words are printed in a small, worn type and are uncertain: "ἀναθήματα", "ςωσφρονεῖ" (second word of item 4), "ἀλογισμάτα", "ἀλλοτρίων" were read from partial glyphs and are marked [?]. The final Greek line after "Menander:" sits at the right and is too faint to read. Long s is printed as s and has been normalised to s. The printed forms "Peruos" and "suæ" were normalised to "Pervos" and "suæ" under rule 5. Printed hyphens at line ends are kept (tem-plo, re-gali, Aqui-lam, felicitér-que, respon-dit, Vi-tauit, trans-lata, no-bis). The page number 136 is at the top left and the running head is HYPOMNEMATA.
